data.content:
GraphRAG
A specific implementation or approach of Retrieval-Augmented Generation that leverages graph-structured data for retrieval.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
A natural language generation technique where a model retrieves relevant information from a knowledge source before generating a response.

Large Language Models (LLMs)
Advanced AI models trained on vast amounts of text data, capable of understanding, generating, and processing human language.

Query-Focused Summarization (QFS)
A task that involves summarizing an entire text corpus to answer global questions, such as identifying main themes in a dataset, rather than retrieving specific localized information.

Vector RAG
A baseline Retrieval-Augmented Generation approach that relies primarily on vector embeddings for retrieval, against which GraphRAG showed substantial improvements.

Knowledge Graph
A structured representation of information where extracted entities become nodes and relationships become edges, aggregated from multiple instances across documents.

Entity Knowledge Graph
A specific type of knowledge graph derived from source documents by an LLM, where nodes represent entities and edges represent relationships between them, forming the first stage of GraphRAG's index building process.

LLM-as-a-judge technique
A novel evaluation methodology, adapted for GraphRAG, which uses one LLM to generate diverse global sensemaking questions and a second LLM to judge the answers of different RAG systems based on predefined criteria.

Sensemaking Queries
Queries that require a global understanding of an entire dataset or corpus, often involving reasoning over connections and implicit concepts to anticipate trajectories and act effectively, which conventional RAG struggles with.

Community Detection
A graph-based analysis technique used in GraphRAG to partition the constructed knowledge graph into a hierarchy of communities of closely related entities, enabling the generation of community-level summaries.

Text Embeddings
A common technique in conventional RAG for representing text records as vectors, where semantic similarity between texts is measured by the closeness of their corresponding vectors in space.

Context Window
The maximum number of tokens (units of text) that a large language model (LLM) can process at once, which dictates the amount of information that can be included in a single prompt.

Microsoft Research
A research division of Microsoft, listed as an affiliation for several authors of the paper.

Microsoft Strategic Missions and Technologies
A division within Microsoft, listed as an affiliation for several authors of the paper.

Microsoft Office of the CTO
A division within Microsoft, listed as an affiliation for several authors of the paper.

GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer)
A family of large language models known for excelling at sensemaking in complex domains and used in various capacities within RAG systems.

Llama
A family of large language models mentioned as capable of sensemaking in complex domains.

Gemini
A family of large language models mentioned as capable of sensemaking in complex domains.

GPT-4
A highly advanced large language model developed by OpenAI, known for its strong performance across various NLP tasks.

LangChain
A software framework designed for developing applications powered by large language models.

LlamaIndex
A data framework designed for LLM applications, facilitating data ingestion, indexing, and querying for building applications like RAG.

NebulaGraph
A distributed, open-source graph database, noted for its integration with GraphRAG for LLM applications.

Neo4J
A leading graph database platform, recognized for its ecosystem tools and support for graph-based applications like GraphRAG.

Louvain algorithm
A widely used algorithm for community detection in graphs, mentioned as a technique for partitioning graphs into nested modular communities.

Leiden algorithm
A community detection algorithm for graphs, mentioned as a technique for partitioning graphs into nested modular communities, building upon the Louvain algorithm.

An author of the paper, affiliated with Microsoft Research, and a co-contributor to the work.

An author of the paper, affiliated with Microsoft Research.

Jonathan Larson
An author of the paper, affiliated with Microsoft Research.

LLM
Acronym for Large Language Model; a type of AI model that processes and generates human-like text, used in the research to produce answers for pairwise comparisons and evaluated based on alignment with claim-based metrics.

RAG Evaluation
The process of assessing the performance of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, particularly focusing on explicit fact retrieval and global sensemaking.

HotPotQA
A sample dataset used to evaluate the impact of chunk size and self-reflection iterations on entity extraction performance with GPT-4.

MultiHop-RAG
A dataset used to demonstrate graph communities detected using the Leiden algorithm.

MT-Bench
A benchmark dataset used for evaluating RAG performance and demonstrating the capability of LLMs as evaluators (Zheng et al., 2024).

vector RAG performance
A specific type of RAG system performance evaluated by existing benchmarks, typically focused on explicit fact retrieval.

global sensemaking
The ability to understand and summarize the entirety of a corpus, which is a key focus of the proposed evaluation approach for RAG systems.

Adaptive benchmarking
A process of dynamically generating evaluation benchmarks tailored to specific domains or use cases, often utilizing LLMs to ensure relevance, diversity, and alignment with target applications.

LLM-based persona generation
A technique where LLMs generate diverse and authentic sets of personas, used in the proposed adaptive benchmarking procedure to create queries representative of real-world RAG system usage.

RAG system
Retrieval Augmented Generation system, a type of system that combines information retrieval with language generation, which is the subject of evaluation in the text.

natural language generation
The field of artificial intelligence focused on generating human-like text, where LLMs have shown to be effective evaluators.

fluency
A criterion for evaluating the quality of generated texts, often quantified by LLMs.

context relevance
A criterion for evaluating RAG systems, specifically related to the relevance of the retrieved context, part of the RAGAS framework.

faithfulness
A criterion for evaluating RAG systems, related to how well the generated answer aligns with the source information, part of the RAGAS framework.

answer relevance
A criterion for evaluating RAG systems, related to how relevant the generated answer is to the query, part of the RAGAS framework.

RAGAS
A framework (Es et al., 2023) that proposes specific criteria like 'context relevance', 'faithfulness', and 'answer relevance' for evaluating vector RAG systems.

LLM-as-a-judge
A methodology where a Large Language Model is used to evaluate the output of other LLMs, often compared with human judgment.

claims
Verifiable factual statements about entities extracted by LLMs, used for validating evaluation results and forming part of the knowledge graph.

GraphRAG Workflow
The high-level data flow and pipeline of the GraphRAG approach, describing its key design parameters and implementation details.

text chunks
Segments into which source documents are split, from which LLMs extract information for downstream processing in the GraphRAG pipeline.

NeoChip
An example company described as specializing in low-power processors for wearables and IoT devices, used to illustrate the process of entity extraction.

NewTech Exchange
An example stock exchange where NeoChip's shares surged, used to illustrate entity extraction.

Quantum Systems
An example company described as having previously owned NeoChip, used to illustrate entity extraction.

in-context learning
A technique (Brown et al., 2020) for LLM prompting where domain-appropriate few-shot exemplars are provided to tailor prompt behavior for specific domains.

named entities
A broad class of entities like people, places, and organizations that can be extracted by LLMs.

abstractive summarization
A type of summarization where meaningful summaries of concepts, relationships, and claims are generated, which may not be explicitly stated in the source text.

entity matching
The task of reconciling different extracted names for the same entity, mentioned as a process in knowledge graph creation.

community detection algorithms
A class of algorithms used to partition a graph into communities of strongly connected nodes, used in the GraphRAG pipeline.

Leiden community detection
A specific community detection algorithm (Traag et al., 2019) used in the GraphRAG pipeline in a hierarchical manner to partition the graph index into groups of elements.

hierarchical community detection
The recursive application of community detection (e.g., Leiden) to detect sub-communities within each detected community until reaching leaf communities, enabling divide-and-conquer summarization.

community hierarchy
A multi-level structure produced by hierarchical community detection, where each level provides a partition of graph nodes, enabling divide-and-conquer global summarization.

Liu
Researcher associated with work on the impact of text chunk size on LLM recall (Liu et al., 2023).

Brown

Barlaug
Researcher associated with work on entity matching (Barlaug and Gulla, 2021).

Gulla
Researcher associated with work on entity matching (Barlaug and Gulla, 2021).

Christen
Researcher associated with work on entity matching (Christen and Christen, 2012).

Elmagarmid
Researcher associated with work on entity matching (Elmagarmid et al., 2006).

Fortunato

Jin

Community Summaries
Summaries generated based on communities detected within the graph index, used as context for answer generation in some experimental conditions (C0-C3).

LLM (Large Language Model)
An artificial intelligence model central to the system, utilized for generating community summaries, global answers, sensemaking questions, and serving as an evaluator for answer quality.

Token Limit
A constraint on the maximum number of tokens an LLM's context window can process, influencing how information is prioritized and summarized within the system.

Global Sensemaking Question Generation
A procedure that employs an LLM to create high-level, corpus-specific questions designed to assess overall understanding of a given text corpus, rather than requiring specific factual recall.

RAG systems (Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems)
A general class of artificial intelligence systems that combine information retrieval with text generation capabilities, evaluated in this research for their effectiveness in global sensemaking tasks.

LLM Evaluator
An application of a Large Language Model used to compare and judge the relative performance of different RAG systems based on predefined criteria like comprehensiveness, diversity, empowerment, and directness.

Comprehensiveness
A metric measured as the average number of claims extracted from answers, indicating how complete the generated answers are.

Diversity
A metric measured by clustering claims for each answer and calculating the average number of clusters, indicating the variety of information in the generated answers.

Empowerment
A metric that evaluates the ability of generated answers to help users reach an informed understanding, often tied to providing specific examples, quotes, and citations.

Directness
A validity test metric used to confirm that vector RAG produces the most direct responses.

Podcast transcripts dataset
A dataset composed of public transcripts from the 'Behind the Tech with Kevin Scott' podcast, used as one of the two corpora for evaluating RAG systems.

News articles dataset
A benchmark dataset containing news articles published between September 2013 and December 2023, used as one of the two corpora for evaluating RAG systems.

Kevin Scott
The Microsoft CTO and host of the 'Behind the Tech' podcast, which is the source for one of the evaluation datasets.

Microsoft
The technology company where Kevin Scott serves as CTO, associated with the 'Behind the Tech with Kevin Scott' podcast data source.

Text Summarization method (TS)
A baseline summarization approach that applies a map-reduce process directly to source texts, used for comparative evaluation against GraphRAG.

Vector RAG 'semantic search' approach (SS)
A baseline RAG implementation that retrieves and adds text chunks to the context window based on semantic similarity until a token limit is reached, used for comparative evaluation.

Map-reduce approach
A general computational pattern involving mapping data into intermediate key-value pairs and then reducing values with the same key, applied in the text summarization (TS) method.

Graph Community Levels (C0, C1, C2, C3)
Hierarchical levels (from root-level C0 to low-level C3) within GraphRAG's community structure, representing different granularities of community summaries used for generating answers.

Graph Index
A data structure created using entity and relationship extraction prompts, supporting conditions C0-C3 by organizing information for answer generation.

Entity and Relationship Extraction
A process used to create the graph index, involving generic prompts with tailored entity types and few-shot examples for a specific domain.

Community Answers
Answers generated using community summaries as context.

Global Answers
Answers generated using a broader scope of information, potentially from the entire graph index or aggregated community summaries.

Podcast Dataset
A collection of podcast transcripts used as one of the primary datasets for the experiments.

Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8171M CPU
A specific CPU model used within a virtual machine to run graph indexing and other computational processes.

OpenAI Endpoint
A public service provided by OpenAI, used to access language models.

gpt-4-turbo
A large language model (LLM) developed by OpenAI, used for answer generation in the experiments.

Leiden Community Detection
An algorithm used for detecting communities within networks or graphs, implemented using the graspologic library.

graspologic library
A software library used to implement Leiden community detection.

Chung et al. (2019)
Researchers whose work is cited in relation to the graspologic library.

Experiment 1
The first experimental setup conducted to validate comprehensiveness and diversity results, comparing global approaches with vector RAG and GraphRAG with source text summarization.

Experiment 2
The second experimental setup, which validated comprehensiveness and diversity results from Experiment 1 using claim-based measures.

Factual Claim
Defined as 'a statement that explicitly presents some verifiable facts,' used as a basis for claim-based measures.

Ni et al. (2024)
Researchers whose definition of a factual claim was used in the study.

Claimify
An LLM-based method or tool designed to identify sentences containing factual claims and decompose them into simple, self-contained factual claims.

Metropolitansky and Larson (2025)
Researchers credited with developing Claimify.

Clustering
A data analysis technique used to group similar factual claims, specifically agglomerative clustering, for measuring diversity.

Padmakumar and He (2024)
Researchers whose approach for clustering was followed in the study.

Scikit-learn
A popular open-source machine learning library for Python, providing various classification, regression, and clustering algorithms.

Agglomerative Clustering
A hierarchical clustering algorithm implemented in Scikit-learn, used for grouping factual claims based on their similarity.

Pedregosa et al. (2011)
Researchers credited with the development or significant contribution to Scikit-learn.

Complete Linkage
A specific linkage criterion used in agglomerative clustering, where clusters are merged only if the maximum distance between their farthest points is below a threshold.

ROUGE-L
A recall-based metric for evaluating summarization and translation, used as a distance metric (1-ROUGE-L) for clustering factual claims.

News Dataset
A collection of news articles used as a dataset for the experiments, alongside the Podcast dataset.

Vector RAG (SS)
A conventional retrieval-augmented generation approach, serving as a baseline (SS condition) for comparison against global approaches like GraphRAG.

Source Text Summarization (TS)
A baseline approach where summaries are generated directly from source texts (TS condition), without using a graph index.

LLM Reasoning
The analytical process performed by a Large Language Model to evaluate aspects like empowerment by analyzing LLM responses.

Graph RAG Conditions (C0-C3)
Specific experimental configurations of the GraphRAG approach, differing in how context is created from the graph index. C0 uses root-level community summaries, while C1-C3 use increasingly finer-grained community summaries.

Root-level Community Summaries (C0)
A specific configuration within GraphRAG conditions (C0) that utilizes highly summarized, root-level community information as context, known for its efficiency.

Iterative Question Answering
A user interaction pattern where questions are asked sequentially, building on previous answers, which GraphRAG aims to support efficiently.

Sensemaking Activity
The cognitive process of understanding complex information, which iterative question answering aims to facilitate.

Claim-based metrics
A set of objective metrics used to provide an outcome for comparing different conditions, against which the LLM's preferred answers were aligned.

Global search conditions
A category of search strategies (including C0, C1, C2, C3) evaluated in the experiments for comprehensiveness and diversity.

C0
Represents an experimental condition, group, or category being analyzed in the research.

C1
Represents an experimental condition, group, or category being analyzed in the research.

C2
Represents an experimental condition, group, or category being analyzed in the research.

C3
Represents an experimental condition, group, or category being analyzed in the research.

TS
Represents a specific measure or variable, possibly 'Task Success' or 'Treatment Score', being quantified across different conditions.

SS
Represents a specific measure or variable, possibly 'Subjective Score' or 'Satisfaction Score', being quantified across different conditions.

Majority voting
A technique used to aggregate results from multiple trials of pairwise comparisons into a single label (winner, loser, or tie) for robust evaluation.

Distance Threshold
A parameter used in evaluation, specifically to define a tie based on the absolute difference between claim-based results for different conditions, and also influencing the average number of clusters.

Fabrication rates
A metric related to the accuracy of generated information, referring to the extent to which an AI system generates false or hallucinated content, suggested as a future evaluation point.

SelfCheckGPT
An approach or model proposed by Manakul et al. (2023) for evaluating fabrication rates in generated text.

Graph index
A core component of the GraphRAG approach, representing the structured organization of information within a knowledge graph, used for efficient retrieval and summarization.

Rich text annotations
A feature of the GraphRAG approach involving additional metadata or information linked to text, enhancing the knowledge graph and supporting retrieval.

Hierarchical community structure
An organizational principle within the GraphRAG approach where information is grouped into communities at different levels, aiding in summarization and exploration.

RAG approaches
A general class of techniques for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, which combine retrieval of relevant information with generative models to produce more accurate and grounded responses.

Embedding-based matching
A technique used in RAG approaches where user queries and graph annotations are matched based on their semantic similarity in an embedding space.

Hybrid RAG schemes
A conceptual extension of RAG approaches that combine different methods, such as embedding-based matching with just-in-time community report generation, to enhance performance.

Map-reduce summarization mechanisms
A summarization technique, often involving distributed processing, used in the GraphRAG approach for generating summaries and also mentioned as a 'global but graph-free approach'.

Knowledge graph generation
The process of creating a knowledge graph, which involves extracting entities and relationships from text, a key component of the GraphRAG approach.

Query-focused summarization (QFS)
A summarization technique that generates summaries tailored to a specific query, combined with knowledge graph generation in the GraphRAG approach.

Average Number of Clusters
A metric reported in the evaluation, indicating the average number of distinct groups identified within the datasets under different conditions and distance thresholds.

Knowledge-augmented language model prompting
A technique for enhancing language models by incorporating external knowledge, often from knowledge graphs, to improve their performance, particularly for zero-shot knowledge graph question answering.

Causal discovery
The process of identifying causal relationships from data, an area where large language models are being explored for advanced capabilities.

Neural networks for entity matching
The application of neural networks to the problem of identifying records that refer to the same real-world entity.

Query focused abstractive summarization
A text summarization technique that generates a concise summary from text, specifically tailored to a given query and focusing on abstracting information.

Community detection in large networks
An algorithm or process for identifying groups of densely connected nodes (communities) within large networks, often referred to as 'fast unfolding'.

Few-shot learners
A characteristic of language models, indicating their ability to learn new tasks effectively with only a small number of training examples.

Retrieval-augmented text generation
A method that combines retrieving relevant information from a knowledge source with a text generation model to produce more informed and accurate outputs.

The data matching process
A general process in data management concerning the identification of corresponding records across different data sources.

Graspy
A Python library for graph statistics, used in machine learning research for analyzing graph data.

DUC 2005
The Document Understanding Conferences 2005, an evaluation campaign for question-focused summarization systems.

Duplicate record detection
The task of identifying redundant or identical records within a dataset, a common problem in data management and quality.

Ragas
A system or framework for automated evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) models.

KnowItAll
A web-scale information extraction system designed to automatically extract facts from the web.

G-retriever
A Retrieval-Augmented Generation model specifically designed for textual graph understanding and question answering.

ForceAtlas2
A continuous graph layout algorithm designed for network visualization, often used with software like Gephi.

Gephi
Graph visualization software, for which ForceAtlas2 is a continuous graph layout algorithm.

Community detection approaches
A general category of methods, ranging from statistical modeling to deep learning, used to identify groups of densely connected nodes in graphs.

Knowledge graph-augmented language models
Language models enhanced by integrating knowledge graphs to improve performance in tasks like knowledge-grounded dialogue generation.

Demonstrate-search-predict
A method for composing retrieval and language models for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks, focusing on demonstrating examples, searching for information, and then predicting an answer.
